children: Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest stepped up bets on biotechnology and AI during the last week, with Meta Platforms
and a group of gene-editing companies among its biggest purchases, while cutting exposure to Alphabet
and several other technology and healthcare names.
Biotechnology was a major focus on the buy side, led by Beam Therapeutics
, with Ark purchasing over 534K shares worth about $14M. The firm also bought ~158K shares of CRISPR Therapeutics
worth $8.5M and 506K shares of Intellia Therapeutics
worth ~$6M. Smaller additions included Scribe Therapeutics
In AI and technology, Meta Platforms
was Ark’s biggest purchase, with 43K shares bought for about $28M. Ark also added over 32K shares of Cerebras Systems
worth $6.5M and a smaller addition to Kratos Defense & Security Solutions
In space and mobility, ARK bought ~576K shares of Archer Aviation
worth ~$3M, with smaller additions to Rocket Lab
. In fintech and crypto, the firm purchased 27K shares of Robinhood Markets
worth $3M, along with smaller additions to the 3iQ Solana Staking ETF (SOLQ.U).
On the sell side, technology sales were led by Alphabet
, with Ark selling 86K shares worth $28.6M. The firm also sold ~19K shares of Advanced Micro Devices
worth $9.9M, $6.5M in Palantir Technologies
and $4.25M in Bullish
stock.
In healthcare, Ark also cut exposure to Twist Bioscience
worth $10.6M, Tempus AI
worth ~$7.9M and 10x Genomics
worth $7.2M. Smaller reductions included GeneDx
and Brera

title: Cathie Wood's Ark weekly recap: buys Meta, gene-editing stocks while cutting Alphabet
